# Fontes

> Fontes is a free, open-source (Apache 2.0) MCP server. It lets any MCP app (Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and others) search court decisions and legislation live on court and government websites in 125 jurisdictions and international courts. Every result names its source and links to the original. It can also show a law as it stood on a past date and read legislation from 91 more countries, using Lexifina's record of the law (not the official publisher).

Facts:

- Runs on the user's computer as a local stdio MCP server. No account, no database, no hosted Fontes service. PyPI package: `fontes-mcp` (Python 3.13+). MCP Registry name: `io.github.ykarapazar/fontes`.
- Works in any app that can run a local stdio MCP server, e.g. Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code (GitHub Copilot), Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Zed, LM Studio, Cline.
- Install: command `uvx fontes-mcp` in any MCP client's settings; `codex mcp add fontes -- uvx fontes-mcp` (Codex); `claude mcp add fontes -- uvx fontes-mcp` (Claude Code); a `.mcpb` file for Claude Desktop. One-click Mac and Windows installers are in the latest GitHub release. `uvx` needs uv.
- Tools: nine research tools, plus `report_bug`: `list_jurisdictions`, `search_caselaw`, `get_decision`, `search_legislation`, `get_legislation_toc`, `get_legislation_provision`, `get_legislation_text`, `get_law_on_date`, `get_law_history`. The jurisdiction is a parameter. `get_law_on_date` and `get_law_history` read Lexifina's record.
- Coverage: 125 live jurisdictions (108 UN member states, 4 other territories, the DIFC Courts, 11 international courts and bodies and the US state courts), read live from court and government websites. 72 of the 125 count as covered under a strict rule (top court precedents, or constitution and primary acts, reached completely). Separately, 91 more countries come from Lexifina's record, legislation only; the two numbers are never added together. Coverage differs a lot between jurisdictions.
- Lexifina (github.com/lexifina/global-law) keeps the law of about 200 countries with every change dated. It is not the official publisher and its record is not live. Every answer from it names Lexifina and links the official publisher's page. For today's text of Dutch and UK legislation and US Code sections, `get_law_on_date` also fetches the official page and says whether Lexifina's record matches it; other countries are not compared. Fontes is not affiliated with Lexifina.
- Most sources are government or court websites; unofficial sources are flagged in each answer.
- API keys: France needs a free PISTE key; US case-law search works better with a free api.data.gov key; US state courts need a free CourtListener token; no other jurisdiction needs one. Sources whose terms need permission are off by default.
- Privacy: searches go to the source being searched. For `get_law_on_date`, `get_law_history`, the 91 Lexifina countries and India's Acts, the search words, citations and dates go to Lexifina's public server (global-law.lexifina.com) as well as, or instead of, the official site; set `WLM_LEXIFINA=0` to turn that off. A daily PyPI version check is on by default (`FONTES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns it off); usage counts and bug reports are opt-in.
- Not legal advice; no legal services are offered. Maintained by one person, Yüce Karapazar; no company, no guarantee. Contact: fontesmcp@proton.me.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykarapazar/fontes/main/README.md): what Fontes does, install, tools, coverage and sources tables
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykarapazar/fontes/main/docs/FAQ.md): official vs unofficial sources, API keys, privacy, legal advice, maintenance, reporting errors
- [Coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykarapazar/fontes/main/docs/COVERAGE.md): per jurisdiction, what is reached, what is not, and why
- [Install guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykarapazar/fontes/main/docs/INSTALL.md): steps for each MCP app
- [Privacy notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ykarapazar/fontes/main/docs/PRIVACY.md): what can leave the user's computer, and when
